operation.coupling: After drawing an i.i.d. sample identifier, the algorithm may reuse it at the points required by the finite-difference template. The same G sample and Gaussian direction also couple the differences at y and z. Fresh samples and internal Gaussian directions are independently drawn as prescribed by the source algorithm.

feedback_quality.description: The response is the exact scalar value of the selected sampled function at the query point. Noise is not added independently at each point: responses at several points are coupled through the same random function. Finite differences are generally unbiased for a smoothed objective and have controlled bias for the original objective.

operation.index_control: The algorithm selects query points, directions, and whether to reuse an already drawn identifier. It cannot choose the outcome of an i.i.d. draw. Every scalar value evaluation is charged individually.

bindings.source_value: arbitrary measurable functions of past responses

This model counts only oracle resources. Arithmetic, linear algebra, and storage applied to received responses are free. Any extra hidden-function gradient, HVP/JVP, value, or inner-solve response must be obtained through a declared, charged operation.

features.label: No additional span restriction explicitly imposed

bindings.source_value: Algorithms may use private randomness. Queries, stopping, and postprocessing may be arbitrary measurable functions of the transcript. The output may be unqueried, a random selection of a past point, or an admissible average. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed. Queries are sequential; each actual response in a parallel batch is charged separately. Arithmetic, linear algebra, and storage using received data are uncharged. Internal operations, memory, and communication are not tracked by this quantity.

Output one outer point $\widehat{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$. An inner solution, function value, or computable accuracy certificate is not required. Arbitrary admissible postprocessing and unqueried outputs are allowed.
accuracy in mathematical expectation/norm; no computed certificate required

Choose one algorithm from the public parameters, then require $\mathbb{E}\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat{x})\|_2^2\le\varepsilon^2$ for every admissible instance and legal oracle law. Expectation includes all algorithmic and feedback randomness, with the instance fixed first.

features.label: Second moment of the complete error

Private algorithmic randomness, including random selection of the output iterate
fixed worst-case total number of calls on every execution
The budget is a fixed worst-case cap on every execution path; every actual response within a batch is counted.
fixed worst-case total number of calls on every execution
Exact real arithmetic is assumed; the stochastic oracle has the stated noise. Bit complexity, memory, and arithmetic cost are not tracked.
